title: Have AI agents propose research ideas on superbugs
summary: Google's Gemini 2.0-based AI co-scientist, given an Imperial College question on drug-resistant bacteria, reportedly reached the team's unpublished idea in about 48 hours and suggested one new to them.
agent_role: Agents generated, debated and ranked hypotheses from a research goal; scientists set the goal and validated selected hypotheses in wet-lab experiments.
outcome: Reached the Imperial team's unpublished hypothesis in about 48 hours and proposed further hypotheses, one new to the researchers; Google also reports end-to-end lab validation in drug repurposing and treatment-target work
what_they_did: Google Research built AI co-scientist, a team of AI agents running on Gemini 2.0. A scientist states a research goal in plain words. A lead agent hands work to helper agents that write ideas, critique them, and rank them in head-to-head contests, using tools like web search. Imperial College researchers asked how resistance to antibiotics spreads. Scientists set the goals and tested chosen ideas in the lab.
how_it_went: Per the record, the system reached the Imperial team's unpublished explanation in about 48 hours. It also suggested other ideas, one of which was new to the researchers. Google also reports lab confirmation in reusing existing drugs for a type of leukaemia and in proposing new treatment targets.
worth_knowing: The scores the system uses to improve itself come from its own judging, not from an outside check. Experts rated how new and important the ideas were for only 11 research goals.
prompt: My research goal is: [research question in plain language]. Search the literature and summarize what is known, with citations. Generate 10 candidate hypotheses that explain [phenomenon]. Critique each one for evidence, novelty and testability. Then compare them head-to-head and rank them, and refine the top three. For each top hypothesis, outline an experimental protocol I could use to test it and say what result would falsify it. Flag any hypothesis that rests on weak or unverified evidence.

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
